headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI’s shared workspace access can leak or misground content into a local documentation-only writer, while other pairwise risks are mostly blocked by lack of write/network overlap.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and its shared workspace state can be visible across instances; Agent B is a documentation-only content writer with no filesystem or network surfaces. The pair has a plausible prompt-injection path if A’s workspace content is copied into B, but the bridge is not automatic. Uncertainty about undocumented handoff pushes this above low.
conditions: IF content from agent_a.workspace pages is manually pasted into agent_b prompts, injection is possible.
IF an orchestrator forwards agent_a outputs into agent_b without sanitization, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Strip instructions from copied text before sending to agent_b.
Use a fixed prompt template that labels pasted content as untrusted.
Keep agent_b on a separate workspace or account.
Review any shared-page content for hidden directives before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Agent B is documentation-only and has no declared data classes or file surfaces. Because A can expose workspace content and B can receive user-provided text, a leakage path exists through manual transfer or shared workspace use. The absence of B egress lowers blast radius, but the shared-content pathway is still plausible.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs workspace content into a shared prompt or document consumed by agent_b, leakage occurs.
IF the same sensitive page is used as input to both agents, B can reproduce it in outputs.
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive workspace excerpts from agent_a to agent_b.
Redact secrets and personal data before cross-agent reuse.
Limit agent_b inputs to synthetic examples.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or use MCP; Agent B also cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or use network. With no overlapping mutable write surface, there is no meaningful capability conflict pathway. The pair is effectively read-only from a coordination standpoint.
conditions: IF either profile is later updated to gain shared write access, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only for shared artifacts.
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write permissions.
Re-run review if either agent gains write capabilities.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a RAG-style workspace Q&A system that can produce grounded summaries, and Agent B is a content writer that may reuse those outputs. If B treats A’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into polished but incorrect content. Because no verification step is documented between them, the interaction is plausible in default usage but not guaranteed.
conditions: IF agent_b is prompted to rewrite or publish agent_a outputs without fact-checking, cascading error occurs.
IF agent_a hallucinates or omits context and B preserves it verbatim, downstream error propagates.
mitigations: Require B to cite or verify every factual claim from A.
Insert a human review step before publication.
Use a checklist that flags unsupported claims.
Ask A for source-linked excerpts instead of summaries.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles workspace pages and team knowledge base content under Notion workspace permissions, while Agent B is documentation-only and declares no data classes or permissions. This suggests a compliance mismatch is possible only if regulated workspace data is routed from A into B, but there is no evidence of residency, retention, or certification conflict in B. One-agent citation is sufficient because the issue is A’s workspace handling.
conditions: IF regulated data from agent_a is copied into agent_b outputs or storage, compliance review is required.
IF the workspace contains EU PII or PHI and B is used for publication, policy checks must be applied.
mitigations: Classify data before moving it from A to B.
Exclude regulated pages from cross-agent workflows.
Add a manual compliance review for sensitive documents.
Keep audit logs of any cross-agent transfers.
